stem: A nurse is interpreting central venous pressure (CVP) in a critically ill client. Which statement is most accurate?

options.A: CVP approximates right atrial pressure and should be interpreted with other clinical and hemodynamic data.
options.B: CVP directly measures glomerular filtration rate.
options.C: A single CVP value reliably measures total circulating blood volume and predicts fluid responsiveness.
options.D: CVP directly measures left ventricular filling pressure and pulmonary venous pressure.

rationale: CVP is measured near the right atrium and can estimate right atrial pressure and aspects of right-sided hemodynamics. It is influenced by several physiologic factors and correlates poorly with total blood volume or fluid responsiveness when used alone. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Interpret CVP as a right-sided pressure estimate rather than a standalone measure of intravascular volume or fluid responsiveness.
source_locator: Introduction; Issues of Concern; Organ Systems Involved
source_claim_supported: CVP estimates right atrial pressure/preload and is influenced by multiple factors; it does not directly correlate with total circulating volume and is a poor standalone predictor of fluid responsiveness.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — hemodynamic monitoring and interpretation of diagnostic data
correction_summary: Retained the clinically correct construct but tightened the language so CVP is described as an estimate/approximation rather than a direct standalone volume measure. Difficulty set to medium.
audit_findings: NCBI directly supports A and specifically describes CVP as a poor standalone predictor of fluid responsiveness. B-D misidentify what CVP measures. Independent second pass passed.
